# Department AI Workflow Planner
**Purpose:** Fill this out for your department before we build your AI tool guide. Your answers let us map the tools to how you actually work - not a generic overview. One file per department, 20-30 minutes to complete.

---

## How to Use This

Answer each question as specifically as you can. You don't need perfect answers - concrete and honest beats thorough and polished. If something doesn't apply to your department, write "N/A." If you genuinely don't know, write "not sure" and we'll figure it out together.

When you're done, send this to Adam. He'll follow up on anything that needs more detail before building your guide.

---

## Section 3: How You Make Decisions

This section is about the judgment calls in your work - when you have to decide what to do next based on the situation.

**Describe one decision you make regularly where the right answer depends on the specific situation.**
Use this format:
- Situation: (what's in front of you)
- You check: (what information or factors do you look at)
- If A: (you do this)
- If B: (you do that)

> Example: "A customer reports a time clock error. I check what model they have and what the error message says. If it's a known error for that model, I send them the fix steps. If it's something I haven't seen before, I escalate to Adam."

>

**Add another if you have one:**
>

**When you're trying to figure out the answer to something - a product question, a customer issue, a policy question - what do you check first? Second?**
> Example: "First I check the Help Center. If it's not there, I ask Tyler or check the Slack #support channel."
>

---

## Section 4: Handoffs

**Are there tasks that get passed to your department from someone else? Who passes them, and what triggers the handoff?**
> Example: "Sales passes us a customer once the contract is signed. We get an email from Andy with the contract attached."
>

**Are there tasks your department starts and then hands off to someone else? What triggers that?**
> Example: "If a support case involves a billing dispute, we hand it to Kelsey. We do that when the customer pushes back more than once."
>

---

## Section 5: What the AI Tools Would Help With

**Walk through one real example where an AI tool would save you time. Use this format:**

- What happened: (what came in or what you needed to do)
- What you did manually: (the steps you took)
- Where the AI could help: (which step could be faster or easier with a tool)
- What the output would be: (what you'd end up with)

> Example: "A customer emailed saying their time clock was frozen. I looked up their device model in Salesforce, searched the Help Center for that error, wrote up the troubleshooting steps, and replied. The AI could look up the device and suggest the right steps so I'm not hunting through the Help Center every time. The output would be a draft reply I can send or adjust."

>

**Is there anything you currently bring to Adam to help figure out that a tool could handle instead?**
>

**What do you spend time on that you wish took less time?**
>

## Section 6: What You'd Never Use AI For

**Are there situations in your department where you should always have a human make the call - no shortcuts?**
> Example: "Any time a customer is threatening to cancel, that conversation needs to stay with a person."
>

- [ ] Financial data (invoices, payment info, contracts)
- [ ] Login credentials, passwords, or access keys
